description: Pure Homomorphic Encryption ablation — FULL model coverage. 100% of parameters (all 20 layers) are CKKS-encrypted client-side before transmission; the server performs the weighted aggregation entirely on ciphertext and never observes plaintext model weights.

why_this_differs_from_the_main_experimen.main_experiment_source: src/data_loader.py's load_partition_network(), called by main.py (Krum/DP-SGD experiments), fit on the FULL corpus (~736,046 rows, no row cap)
why_this_differs_from_the_main_experimen.this_run_source: docker_fl/build_partitions.py, invoked with --max-rows 100000 per the script's documented usage example, producing a ~100k-row stratified subsample of the corpus BEFORE VarianceThreshold(threshold=1e-6) is fit
why_this_differs_from_the_main_experimen.root_cause: VarianceThreshold's selected feature set is sample-size-dependent by construction. Several borderline-variance columns that clear the 1e-6 threshold when fit on the full 736,046-row corpus fall below that threshold when fit on a much smaller ~100,000-row stratified subsample. Both code paths run identical preprocessing logic (data_loader.py's load_and_preprocess), differing only in how many rows they operate on before VarianceThreshold is fit — this is not a pipeline bug.
why_this_differs_from_the_main_experimen.resolution_status: NOT YET RESOLVED as of this manifest. Rebuild via 'python build_partitions.py --model-type network --num-clients 2' (omitting --max-rows) to bring this ablation to 38 features and match the main experiment.

dp_config_present_but_inactive.note: these are argparse defaults recorded in config regardless of use_dp; dp_method: null confirms DP genuinely did not execute this run

resource_limits.CONFIRMED_MISMATCH: client.py's own config.mem_limit_mb field reads 200 for BOTH clients in this run, directly contradicting the 500m actually enforced via docker-compose.yml's mem_limit setting. This is a hardcoded label in client.py, not a live read of the real cgroup limit. Any table citing 'headroom under the 200MB constraint' using this run's data would be citing a limit that was not actually in effect (peak usage of ~373-374MB would in fact have EXCEEDED a genuine 200MB limit and caused an OOM kill, which did not happen — confirming 500m was the real, active limit). Fix client.py to read the real limit (e.g. from an env var or /sys/fs/cgroup) before this field is trusted in any report.
